::: {#sol-sharpen}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
z = torch.tensor([2.0, 1.0, 0.0])
divisors = [0.5, 1.0, 2.0]
softened = [torch.softmax(z / d, dim=0) for d in divisors]
first = [p[0].item() for p in softened]
print(softened)
# The prose below says dividing by 0.5 gives the first symbol the most.
assert first[0] > first[1] > first[2]
```

Dividing by 0.5 gives the first symbol probability `r sprintf("%.2f", py$first[[1]])`,
against `r sprintf("%.2f", py$first[[2]])` for $\vz$ itself and `r sprintf("%.2f", py$first[[3]])` for $\vz / 2$.
Dividing by a number below 1 spreads the [logits](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-logits) apart,
which moves probability to the largest;
dividing by a number above 1 brings them together,
which moves the probabilities toward $1/3$ each.

:::
